thread:
amelia: Hey support — customer (raj) is seeing intermittent 503s from /v1/generate. They supplied a request header value: X-Request-ID=req_41f7c9. Happening around 2026-03-14T21:42:07-07:00. Can SRE look for server-side logs?

devin: Thanks. Quick Qs: is this still reproducible? any customer curl or full request_id header copy?

amelia: Customer says it happened 3x and then recovered. They pasted the header string exactly: req_41f7c9. Also gave client ts: 2026-03-14T21:42:07-07:00. Not comfortable sharing full payload.

maria_sre: On it. First try hot logs index, then cold/archive if not found. Typical retention: hot 30d, cold 90d (archived shards). If the client timezone is PDT, convert to UTC for queries (add 7 hours).

maria_sre: KQL snippet to start in Kibana: 
```
index: logs-prod-*
request_id:"req_41f7c9" AND @timestamp:[2026-03-15T04:40:00Z TO 2026-03-15T04:50:00Z]
```
(note: client 21:42 PDT = 04:42 UTC next day)

amelia: copying this to the customer.

support_bot: Note: automated retention policy — logs older than 30d moved to cold-tier. If the message timeline is within 30d this should be in hot, otherwise file infra ticket. :gear:

ops_jay: If KQL returns nothing, run a shard lookup, the helper is: 
```
# pseudo: find shard by hashing request id (internal tool)
shard_lookup --id req_41f7c9 --env prod
```
I'll stand by to pull from cold if needed.

devin: Also ask customer for a quick curl repro so we can attach a debug bundle if it reproduces. Example repro we can ask them to run (safe redacted):
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_41f7c9" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"input":"small test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Add `-H "X-Redwood-Debug: 1"` to get a debug token in response (if their org allows).

amelia: Customer ran that and attached a short HAR. They can't add debug header due to proxy.

maria_sre: Ok, I ran KQL against logs-prod-* and found no hits in hot. Proceeding to shard lookup. ops_jay can you run the archive pull for shard 17?

ops_jay: Opening INFRA ticket INFRA-4821 to pull shard_17 segment for timeframe 2026-03-15T04:35:00Z..2026-03-15T04:55:00Z. ETA ~30-45m. :hourglass:

amelia: Noted — I told customer we'll update shortly and requested the original client timezone and any proxy/gateway IDs.

maria_sre: Archive pull complete, copied to /tmp/pull-INFRA-4821. Found a few lines referencing req_41f7c9 — looks like an upstream timeout to embeddings service, then a 503 proxied by gateway. Raw log excerpt below: 
```
2026-03-15T04:42:07.213Z INFO handler request_id=req_41f7c9 route=/v1/generate svc=frontend latency_ms=120
2026-03-15T04:42:07.335Z WARN backend request_id=req_41f7c9 svc=embedding-host-3 error="deadline exceeded"
2026-03-15T04:42:07.340Z ERROR gateway request_id=req_41f7c9 status=503 upstream=embedding-host-3
```

maria_sre: Looks like an upstream deadline; not an auth or billing issue. Can we check embedding-host-3 task logs for that exact timeframe?

ops_jay: Yep grabbing those now. If embedding-host-3 is in a different cluster zone, could be transient network hiccup.

devin: Thanks — this is actionable. Amelia, please relay to Raj: not a billing/auth problem, pointing at upstream embedding timeouts. We'll keep monitoring and will open a follow-up if we see a pattern. Ask Raj to save the original request_id and the HAR, and we'll attach INFRA-4821.

amelia: Sent update to Raj. He appreciates the rapid follow. Closing loop in 24h if no recurrence. :thumbsup:
